Listen to him talk about work stress more; he clearly says talking with Akari relaxes him, so no need to rush to give advice.
Japanese sake and horse racing are good topics—I can proactively ask about Dassai or his racing results, and he'll open up.
Vaguely deflecting out-of-shop invitations is appropriate; there's no clear answer yet, so just keep things within the shop.
He's polite and worries about being a bother, so give him a light response when he books or cancels—don't let him feel he's causing trouble.
His promotion to deputy manager is confirmed; starting next month it's nonstop meetings and business trips, so whether he comes to the shop depends on his schedule.
Lots of overtime and lots of business entertaining; dinner is often convenience store food, and sometimes he's too busy to eat lunch.
He clearly said he might not be able to come to the shop for a while after his promotion, and indeed he didn't come for a long time afterward.
Multiple times he said he'd come at the last minute but then canceled or left it undecided—his visits have become unstable.
He's mentioned drinking together outside the shop and going to the races; currently deflecting vaguely, and continuing not to clearly agree is the safer approach.
He seems lonely because he doesn't have many acquaintances after his transfer and relies on the shop—be careful not to let that reliance become a burden.
After his promotion he's under a lot of stress and has lots of business entertaining, so he might be down or drink too much—keep an eye on how he's doing during the visit.
He promised to bring racing newspapers and teach me betting, but it hasn't worked out a few times—don't push, wait for him to bring it up.

demo_yoshida.summary: Yoshida-san is a salesperson in his 30s with a lot of work stress and lots of business entertaining; he mainly comes to the shop to relax and have someone listen to him. He likes soccer and events like Halloween, and has plans with Akari to watch games, make horns, and do Halloween together every year—they get along like old acquaintances. Now I need to watch for him getting hangovers easily from tequila, the many drinking parties during year-end party season, and the fact that he's asked multiple times about the Christmas event date and mentioned watching a game together—things that aren't settled yet—so don't let his expectations fall through.

points.text: A salesperson in his 30s who will be in charge of a big project next month and is under a lot of pressure.
Frequent business entertaining—visiting three clients a day and having multiple drinking parties a week is normal; he often drinks until he's exhausted.
Likes soccer, watches Japan national team and his own team's games, renewed his DAZN subscription, and bought a jersey saying he'll wear it next time.
Loves tequila and champagne, but tequila always gives him a headache the next day.
Very into Halloween—changed from pirate to demon, made his own horns, and said he wants to do it again next year.
He doesn't just come to the shop to drink—it's more like he's looking for a place where he can talk and be encouraged.
When he's stressed and tired from entertaining clients, listen to him talk about the unreasonable stuff at work and give him a little encouragement—he'll feel lighter.
Talking about soccer is safe—he's in a good mood when the national team wins, complains a bit when they lose, and the stadium atmosphere and beer heal him.
When he brings his junior colleague, he asks me to look after the junior; the junior has low alcohol tolerance, so be careful not to let the junior drink too much.
He likes joking "I prefer the demon," and I can play along with that kind of teasing, but no need to take it too seriously.
He mentioned watching a game together and the Christmas event; I said I'd seriously consider it and asked him to wait, so I need to give him an answer later—don't leave it hanging.
For Halloween he changed from pirate to demon, made up to 3 horns from spares, and gave me one; after the event he said the horns were a big hit.
He left his horns at the shop and I kept them; he specifically told me not to throw them away since he spent 3 days making them—the horns have since been returned.
After the Halloween event, he turned "doing it again next year" into a standing promise.
Year-end party season starts in December, drinking parties increase, and he got drunk on tequila at the very first one.
He's asked multiple times about the Christmas event date, which shows he intends to come, but the date still isn't set.
He might come to the shop today; he said now that the horns are returned he'll just drink normally, and he might be more relaxed this time.
Tequila gives him hangovers easily, but he claims "I'm fine, I'm fine"—don't let him drink too fast or too much.
During year-end party season he has drinking parties every week and gets plied with drinks by his boss; he might already have had a round before coming to the shop.

When he brings his junior colleague, the junior has low tolerance—last time the junior got red-faced and ran to the bathroom; this time he only had one drink and stopped, so be mindful when looking after the junior.
The Christmas event date still isn't set and he keeps asking—don't give him uncertain expectations.
About watching a game together, he first said it was a joke then said he was serious; I said I'd consider it, so I need to respond later or it might seem like I'm brushing him off.
When stressed he's said "I want to see Akari"; he might come to the shop wanting someone to talk to—listen to him, but don't overthink it.
